summary: Brigitte Steinmann works in Tibetology and related fields. She studied under Alexander W. Macdonald and traditional teacher Bahadur Singh, and held a post at the University of Montpellier (attested 2004).

Bronwyn Finnigan specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Educated at the Universities of Sydney, Melbourne, and Auckland (studying under Rosalind Hursthouse and John Bishop), she held posts at Auckland, Marquette University, and the Australian National University.

Brook Ziporyn works in Sinology, philosophy, and religious studies. Educated at the University of Chicago and the University of Michigan, he held faculty posts at Northwestern University, the National University of Singapore, and the University of Chicago.
Brooke Schedneck is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Arizona State University, where she studied under doctoral supervisor Juliane Schober.

Bruce B. Lawrence is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. Educated at Fay School, Princeton University, and the Episcopal Divinity School, he served on the faculty at Duke University from around 1971 until retiring as professor emeritus.

Bruce Cameron Hall specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned his PhD from Harvard University in 1980 and served as an assistant editor at the College of William & Mary (attested 1987).

Bruce Charles Williams is a scholar in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Edward H. Schafer, Michael C. Rogers, Michel Strickmann, Barend A. van Nooten, Padmanabh S. Jaini, and Akira Fujieda.
Bruce Chilton works in religious studies. He studied at St John's College (~1974–1977) and later held posts at Yale University (~1985–1987) and Bard College (~1987).

Bruce John Stewart specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sakya College and Columbia University (PhD attested 1983), learning from doctoral supervisor Alex Wayman as well as Joel Peter Brereton and Christopher S. George.

Bruce Kapferer is a scholar of religious studies and other fields who studied at the University of Sydney and the University of Manchester. He held posts at Adelaide, UCL, James Cook University, Bergen, and Gothenburg.

Bruce Lincoln is a historian of religions and scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Haverford and the University of Chicago under Mircea Eliade, he held faculty posts at the University of Minnesota and the University of Chicago.

Bruce M. Knauft is an anthropologist and scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Michigan (~1976–1983) and held a professorship at Emory University beginning around 1985.
Bruce M. Sullivan is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He studied under J. A. B. van Buitenen from around 1975 to 1979 and held a post at Northern Arizona University beginning around 1988.

Bruce Matthews works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. After studying at McMaster University, he held posts as a Commonwealth Fellow at the University of Ceylon (~1971–1973) and as a professor at Acadia University (~1976–2006).

Bruce McCoy Owens specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He held appointments at Columbia University (attested 1988) and as an associate professor of anthropology at Wheaton College (attested 2019).

Bruno Dagens was an Indologist, historian, and archaeologist who studied under Colette Caillat. He held posts at the EFEO, KU Leuven, the French Institute of Pondicherry, and Sorbonne Nouvelle University.
Bruno Galasek is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Bonn under the supervision of Konrad Klaus (attested 2016).

Bruno Liebich was an Indologist who studied under Franz Kielhorn and attended the universities of Munich, Göttingen, and Breslau. He held professorships in Indology at the University of Breslau and Heidelberg University.

Bruno Lindner was a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Leipzig and under Rudolf von Roth, later serving as Privatdocent at Leipzig from 1878 to 1919.

Bruno Petzold was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. Educated at Leipzig and Berlin, and by Hikoshiro Hoshino and Daito Shimaji, he taught at the First Higher School, Chuo University, Rissho University, and Seikei High School.
